notes: After two concurrent rotate() calls with the same token: (1) one call succeeded, (2) the other threw TokenReuseDetected, (3) isFamilyRevoked() returned true. The family was erroneously revoked by a legitimate concurrent request.

The second UPDATE in revokeFamily() did NOT sweep the new token row — it was inserted AFTER revokeFamily() ran (the winner's async user lookup + JWT signing runs between the loser's revokeFamily call and the winner's insert). The new token row exists but is unreachable because the family record is revoked (confirmed by E3).

Exactly one rotate() succeeded, one threw TokenReuseDetected. token_families.revoked_at is non-null (family revoked). One token row has revoked_at IS NULL (the new token from the winner) but it is blocked by the revoked family. Using the winner's new token with rotate() throws InvalidToken — the user is permanently locked out of their session.
